questions.question: State the Arrhenius and Brønsted-Lowry definitions of acids and bases, and use the dissolution of ammonia in water to show why the Brønsted-Lowry definition is the more powerful one.
questions.expected_answer: Arrhenius: an acid produces hydrogen ions (H⁺) when dissolved in water, and a base produces hydroxide ions (OH⁻). Brønsted-Lowry: an acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor. Ammonia exposes the weakness of Arrhenius: NH₃ contains no hydroxide, yet its solution is basic. The equation NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ shows ammonia accepting a proton from water to become ammonium, while the water that donated the proton becomes hydroxide. Under Brønsted-Lowry, ammonia is a base because it accepts a proton — the hydroxide in the solution is manufactured from water at the moment of the transfer rather than carried in ammonia's own formula, which the Arrhenius definition could not explain. Arrhenius also confines acid-base behaviour to water, while Brønsted-Lowry does not.

questions.question: Define a conjugate acid-base pair and identify both pairs in HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻. Then show, with two equations, that the hydrogen carbonate ion HCO₃⁻ is an ampholyte.
questions.expected_answer: A conjugate acid-base pair is two species that differ by exactly one proton, the species with the extra proton being the acid. In HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻: pair one is HCl (acid) and Cl⁻ (its conjugate base), since HCl donated a proton to become chloride; pair two is H₃O⁺ (acid) and H₂O (its conjugate base), since water accepted a proton to become hydronium. The pairs connect diagonally across the arrow — the two reactants are never a pair. HCO₃⁻ as an ampholyte: acting as an acid (proton donor), HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺; acting as a base (proton acceptor), HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ + OH⁻. Because it can donate a proton in one reaction and accept one in another, it is amphiprotic.

questions.question: Write balanced equations for hydrochloric acid reacting with sodium hydroxide, with magnesium oxide, and with sodium carbonate, naming the products of each. Then give the colours of bromothymol blue and phenolphthalein in acidic, neutral (where applicable) and basic solutions.
questions.expected_answer: With a metal hydroxide: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O — sodium chloride and water. With a metal oxide: 2HCl + MgO → MgCl₂ + H₂O — magnesium chloride and water. With a metal carbonate: 2HCl + Na₂CO₃ → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ — sodium chloride, water and carbon dioxide; the carbonate reaction is the only one that fizzes, and the gas is carbon dioxide. All three follow the master pattern acid + base → salt + water, with carbonates adding CO₂. Bromothymol blue is yellow in acid, green in a neutral solution and blue in base — the only required indicator with a distinct neutral colour. Phenolphthalein is colourless in acid and pink in base; in a neutral solution it remains colourless.
